caption_used: Distribution of Quantifiers and Operations in Categorical, Approximate Number Generation, and Disjunctive & Conjunctive Reasoning. The Categorical pie chart comprises four segments: Universal Quantifiers (29.07%), Negation (27.91%), Limiter (27.91%), and Existential Quantifiers (15.12%). In the Approximate Number Generation chart, Comparative Relationships constitute the largest share at approximately 48%, followed by Approximate Quantities at 33.26% and Absolute Absence at 18.71%. The Disjunctive & Conjunctive chart shows a near-even split, with Conjunctive slightly dominating at 54.51% over Disjunctive at 45.49%.
raw_response:
The figure displays three side-by-side pie charts representing the distribution of quantifiers and operations across three categories: "Categorical", "Approximate Number Generation", and "Disjunctive &Conjunctive". The first chart, titled "Categorical", contains four slices labeled directly within the segments with bold text: "Universal Quantifiers" at 29.07% (light blue-grey), "Limiter" at 27.91% (light pink), "Negation" at 27.91% (light orange), and "Existential Quantifiers" at 15.12% (light green). The second chart, titled "Approximate Number Generation", consists of three slices arranged in descending order of size clockwise from the top right: "Approximate Quantities" at 45.03% (light beige), "Comparative Relationships" at 36.26% (light blue), and "Absolute Absence" at 18.71% (light purple). The third chart, titled "Disjunctive &Conjunctive", is divided into two nearly equal slices: "Conjunctive" at 50.49% (light pinkish-purple) on the right and "Disjunctive" at 49.51% (light blue-grey) on the left. None of the charts include a separate legend, as all category labels and exact percentage values are placed directly inside their respective pastel-colored segments, and there are no visually emphasized, exploded, or offset slices.
